title: Certify the six-call ternary quaternion pair minimum (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Finite exact certificate: `diag([i^-1],[j^-1])` has minimum **six** positive-i/j calls over the full formal algebra `F3[Q8]`, with two arbitrary dirty roles, all ternary rank-one idempotent couplings and free `GL2(F3)` scalar mixing. This excludes a ternary sharing gain at this endpoint. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

```text
12 ternary projectors -> 24 paid factors
forward ball through two calls: 491 full matrices
reverse ball through two calls: 491 full matrices
intersection: empty
odd lengths: excluded by determinant characters
six calls: attained by i^3 on role one, j^3 on role two
```

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Aaron Wang #1822/#2318 for the binary Q8 pair model and exact-search direction; eumemic #288, woklerx #1443, Ali Romman #468, Gareth Davidson #1333 and the retained register-model lineage. The binary results are cited, not replayed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19144877). Canonical main was refreshed unchanged at `a5df48c55ea806d7952b65acc9c76d878ff09b13`, priority revision 7. The bit-new-register-model card changes to this coefficient-field side question. Live PRs and claims, recent same-account contributions, distinctive main-tree and merged-PR searches were checked before committing. Cached coverage was 331 open PRs and 4,359 Discussion records; sparse local-note coverage and unpublished work remain limitations.

## Evidence

Before, the credited binary census leaves this ternary projector alphabet unclassified. After, complete exact meets in two different arithmetic implementations establish the new minimum six. The formal-coefficient implementation and a separate Hamilton-quaternion 16-by-16 regular-action implementation agree on both full state sets. Each ball has layers `(1,24,466)` from 600 transitions. The regular representation is faithful as an algebra action; no smaller quotient is used to accept endpoints.

Both implementations replay the six-call endpoint, reject all six single-call omissions and find a planted four-call target. The primary checker also enumerates all 81 scalar matrices, all 48 scalar invertibles and 576 conjugations, all 512 group associativity triples, gate inverses and determinant-character fixtures. The written argument proves scalar normalization, parity and meet completeness. The generated receipt binds all six other package files by SHA256.

Locally passed on CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64:

- Four registered warning-strict ordinary/optimized commands. Recorded single-run elapsed times: 0.0367, 0.0361, 0.0903 and 0.0839 seconds, all under the 60-second registered limit.
- `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, plus seven-file `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` with source-history checking at `2f98b7ec3e092e1299a9190af6ae45372497137f`.
- Official export/integrity checks and optimized read-only Git-free replay of both implementations with an empty PATH. All eight exported files remained unchanged.
- Five actual optimized-CLI rejection controls for a false minimum, Boolean count alias, false ball digest, duplicate JSON key and changed source bytes. In-memory Python compilation and staged whitespace checks also pass. Ruff was unavailable; warning-strict execution was the available Python diagnostic check.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/ternary-q8-negative-pair/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/ternary-q8-negative-pair/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/ternary-q8-negative-pair/regular.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/ternary-q8-negative-pair/regular.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/ternary-q8-negative-pair
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/ternary-q8-negative-pair --check-source-history
```

Any CPython 3.12 installation can replace the interpreter path. No external Python dependency or predecessor executable is required. Expected scientific markers are `PASS_TERNARY_Q8_NEGATIVE_PAIR minimum=6` and `PASS_TERNARY_Q8_REGULAR_ACTION ... minimum=6`.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

Exactly two roles, scalar field F3, positive labels i/j and this one endpoint. No extra-role or arbitrary-field lower bound is claimed. This is a finite exact certificate with written normalization/parity steps, not a complete multiplication theorem.

Physical ternary address realization, scalar-map charges, source access, restoration, frames, hosting, precision/tape, stock and recursive supplier admission remain unknown. Lean, Docker, predecessor scientific replays and selected cold replay were unrun. Every registered package check ran locally; none is deferred to CI. Managed Python allocation has fixed-domain capacity bounds documented in the README.

## Open next questions

- Does minimum six survive arbitrary finite restored dirty ternary roles? Start with a role-uniform invariant or a complete three-role word; the two-role meet supplies no workspace theorem.
- Can four calls be excluded over every odd field? Determinant parity leaves only label counts `(1,3)` and `(3,1)`, but the finite projector inventory changes with the field.

## Related open work

- #3906 audits binary Q8 dirty-spectator restoration for earlier mixed-negative witnesses. It uses F2 and supplies no competing ternary two-role minimum.
- #2444 supplies binary noncommuting search tooling and Q8 calibration alongside its separate KB2 screen. The ternary scalar-field endpoint here is outside its binary domain.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated. Seven files in one new research package; shared code, frozen predecessors, credit lines and the selected record are unchanged.
